title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: AI prompt and response messages visible for anonymised users
summary: Hold: the scope section presents all three alert-investigating role groups as seeing the change, but Microsoft has not documented which groups can read the new AI messages. The roadmap facts and published governance controls check out; the assertion that the capability takes no action of its own also needs narrowing.

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management now permits review of underlying risky AI prompt and response interactions even when usernames are anonymised.
claims.quote: Customers can now access and review the underlying risky prompt and response interactions generated by users during AI usage, even when user anonymization is enabled within Insider Risk Management investigations.

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management scores risky user activities and supports alerts and investigation cases.
claims.quote: The system automatically calculates alert risk scores from several risk activity indicators.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented which alert-investigating role groups can open this new message view for anonymised users.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Insider Risk Management" "prompt" "Analysts" "view"'; '"Insider Risk Management" "anonymized" "messages"'. Read permissions, privacy, activities and Content explorer; none specifies role access to the new anonymised-user message view.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: Username anonymisation is configured in the Purview portal at Settings > Insider Risk Management > Privacy > Show anonymized versions of usernames.
claims.quote:
Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page.
Select Insider Risk Management to go to the Insider Risk Management settings.
Select Privacy.
Select the option you want, to show anonymized names or not.

claims.claim: Show anonymized versions of usernames replaces a name such as Grace Taylor with a pseudonym such as AnonIS8-988 in the Insider Risk Management experience.
claims.quote: For example, a user 'Grace Taylor' appears with a randomized pseudonym such as 'AnonIS8-988' in all areas of the Insider Risk Management experience.

claims.claim: The username anonymisation setting applies to all Insider Risk Management policies.
claims.quote: Choosing this setting anonymizes all users with current and past policy matches and applies to all policies.

claims.where: What's changing: metadata and file content
claims.claim: Names appearing in activity metadata and within file content in Content explorer are not anonymised.
claims.quote: However, names of users that appear in the metadata of an activity, in the metadata of files in Content explorer, and within content of files in Content explorer aren't anonymized.

claims.claim: Username anonymisation is not preserved for alerts exported with the exporting API.
claims.quote: anonymization of usernames isn't preserved for exported alerts when using the exporting API or when exporting to Microsoft Purview eDiscovery solutions.

claims.claim: Username anonymisation is not preserved for alerts exported to Microsoft Purview eDiscovery.
claims.quote: anonymization of usernames isn't preserved for exported alerts when using the exporting API or when exporting to Microsoft Purview eDiscovery solutions.

Activity: Type of activity taken on an item. Values are Viewed, Deleted, Added, Edited policy, Case, User, Alert, and Settings.
Category: Category of the item modified. Values are Policies, Cases, Users, Alerts, Settings, and Notice templates.

claims.where: What's changing: Microsoft Learn does not describe this capability yet
claims.claim: Learn does not yet specifically describe the new AI interaction message view for anonymised IRM users.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Insider Risk Management" "anonymized" "messages"'; '"AI interaction messages" "Insider" "enable"'. Read privacy, permissions, activities and Content explorer; AI content is mentioned, but this new anonymised-user view is not specifically described.

claims.claim: The capability introduces no change in actions and takes no action of its own.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Insider Risk Management" "viewing" "messages" "automatic"'. Read roadmap and activities documentation. They describe access and review, not a guarantee of no autonomous actions or an unchanged action model.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: 'The roadmap describes this capability as access to and review of underlying risky AI prompt and response interactions.'

claims.claim: The new message-viewing capability is visible to members of all three role groups that can investigate alerts.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Insider Risk Management" "prompt" "Analysts" "view"'. Read permissions, activities and Content explorer. Alert access is documented for three groups, but no passage grants each group this new message view; the briefing itself says that mapping is unknown.
claims.fix: Change the Scope bullet label from 'Who sees it' to 'Who can investigate alerts'. Retain the documented alert and Content explorer role permissions, and append: 'Microsoft has not documented which of these role groups can read the new AI interaction messages for anonymised users.'
